text:
maria: Heads up — we started seeing 99th/95th latency spikes in eu-west dedicated pool around 08:12 UTC. spikes correlate with tenant `glacier` traffic after they rolled quantized model v2.
raj: saw the alert, digging into traces now. p95 tokens/sec drops, GPU util fine but PCIe congestion counters jumping.
ken: PCIe? any NVLink weirdness or host-side DMA storms?
sophie: quick dump from affected host:
```
# nvidia-smi dmon -s u
gpu   mem   enc   dec
2     92    0     0
```
plus `ethtool -S ens192 | grep tx_` shows egress packet bursts.
raj: also seeing increased MMIO retries on /proc/interrupts on that node — looks like cross-socket traffic amplifying during those requests.
zhen: this is consistent with our earlier PCIe crosslink echo issue, but that was mostly noisy batch jobs. glacier is small-chat-size but very bursty with many short sessions.
infra-bot: incident created INC-2026-1784 (auto). Severity: P2.
maria: initial hypothesis: quantized model changed memory access patterns -> more small KV fetches -> more DMA bursts -> host NIC/PCIe contention -> other tenants in same rack see tail latency.
ken: could also be an artifact of kernel driver coalescing with vgpu or MIG contexts. Are they on multi-tenant MIG nodes?
raj: yes, 3/5 affected are MIG partitions on same PGPU host. We should check IOMMU grouping and PF/VF mapping.
sophie: running fio-like KV probe gave this pattern: many tiny DMA reads ~4-8kb at 60-120rps, interleaved. CPU irq handling spikes too.
zhen: mitigation idea: apply per-tenant egress shaping at the socket level (iptables tc or eBPF) to tamp down burstiness while we root-cause. Also consider temporary pinning of glacier to a warm isolated slice (fractional dedicated).
maria: can we do a fast canary: move 1 glacier allocation to an isolated slice in eu-west and observe?
ops: I can schedule a migration now; ETA 10m. Which allocation ID?
raj: allocation a-3387 (eu-west1b). Ops: please move that one and keep others.
ops: moving a-3387 -> isolated-slice-euw1b-3, will monitor.
(5m later)
ops: migration done. initial 1min tail latency dropped ~45% for that allocation. other glacier tenants still noisy.
ken: confirms noisy tenant effect. Next short-term steps: 1) apply soft egress shaping to glacier class (limit burst to 200mbps per-tenant socket) 2) roll one more allocation into isolated-slice 3) gather perf counters (PCIe errs, MMIO retries, NIC queue depths).
sophie: will create a telemetry job to capture NVLink/PCIe counters and NIC qdepth for 10m after shaping.
raj: assigning action items: @zhen follow up with kernel bug/driver team on MMIO retry pattern; @maria coordinate with glacier engineering to throttle client-side burst; @ken run probe to confirm MIG->host mapping amplifies bursts.
zhen: opening ticket DRIVER-2026-412 for vendor follow-up with repro.
infra-bot: runbook step applied: soft isolate tag `sandbagged` applied to glacier.
maria: cost note — isolating tenants increases egress cost by ~12% for that pool. we should surface to finance if we keep it for >24h.
ken: long-term: we should add per-MIG PCIe telemetry and a scheduler policy to avoid colocating high-burst small-rpc tenants on same host. maybe a "burst-averse" placement label.
sophie: Agreed. will draft RFC for placement label and egress shaping knobs. target: canary next week.
maria: TL;DR: noisy tenant `glacier` -> quantized model changed I/O pattern -> PCIe/NIC bursts -> cross-tenant tail latency. Short-term: soft egress shaping + isolate some allocations. Monitoring + vendor ticket open. Next update in #eng-infra in 3h or when DRIVER-2026-412 has vendor response. :thumbsup:
